To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the performance of the weighing gauge is worse than that of the traditional tipping bucket rain gauge under unsteady state (real-world) conditions; (ii) the weighing gauge performance is worse than that obtained by the traditional tipping bucket gauge even if the sampling errors are corrected.

1. the WG investigated in this study does not show a significantly better performance than a traditional TBR under time varying reference rainfall conditions; 2. the WG investigated does not show a significant improvement of the performance with respect to the TBR when corrections for the sampling error are not applied.
the weighing rain gauge investigated under laboratory simulated time-varying reference rainfall rates does not provide better performance than traditional tipping bucket rain gauges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of the performance of the weighing gauge in case of real world rainfall conditions.
the evaluation of the performance of a modern weighing rain gauge under unsteady state (real world) reference rainfall conditions.

the evaluation of the performance of a modern weighing instrument under unsteady state conditions, which are representative of real world applications, and with the development of a suitable rainfall generator for the purpose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the weighing gauge is not a good choice for the measurement of high resolution RI time series, at least in the low and medium intensity range.

the performance of weighing gauge is not superior to TBRs in the low intensity range and under unsteady state conditions, at least under the investigated test conditions and for the investigated instruments.
the WG investigated in this paper does not provide better performances than the TBR under the laboratory conditions here considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of weighing gauges under real conditions is still an open issue and that further investigations are needed.
the WG is not a suitable instrument for high resolution rainfall intensity measurements in case time varying reference conditions are involved.
the performance of weighing gauges under time variable reference rainfall rates is not satisfactory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of WG, a significant sampling error is introduced by the measurement system, which is more relevant than the systematic error associated with the response time of a weighing gauge.

the performance of weighing gauges under real world time varying reference intensities cannot be inferred from the results of laboratory tests performed under steady state reference flow conditions, as is often done in the literature.

, in order to be able to use the WG for hydrological applications where high resolution rainfall intensity data are required, the instrument needs to be properly corrected for sampling and response time related errors.
